news.title: South Sudan Courts Oil Investors as Sudan’s Warring Forces Take Their Share
news.summary: South Sudan is courting fresh capital for 14 exploration blocks and a production increase from roughly 170,000 barrels per day to 230,000, which investors would find impossible to control once those barrels left the country. Captive to neighboring Sudan’s civil war, South Sudan is essentially divvying up its oil, under duress, between the Sudanese Army and the rival paramilitary RSF, which extract payment before the oil can reach the Red Sea. The government-backed South Sudan Oil & Power conference will put that proposition before investors…

analysis.summary: South Sudan seeks investment to expand production while facing transit extortion and disruptions from Sudan's civil war.
analysis.rationale: Proposed production increases from 170,000 to 230,000 bpd exert downward pressure, but active extortion and transit vulnerabilities from Sudan's conflict present ongoing supply disruption risks.

news.title: API Shows Sharp Build in US Crude Oil, Distillate Inventories
news.summary: The American Petroleum Institute (API) estimated that crude oil inventories in the United States rose by 9.0 million barrels in the week ending November 6. In the week prior, US crude oil inventories fell by 5.267 million barrels. Commercial crude oil inventories excluding the SPR have lost more than 54 million barrels over the last 30 weeks, and 3 million over this year, according to API data, which has been kept in check in part thanks to draws from the SPR. For the week ending November 6, 2.7 million barrels of crude oil left the SPR to aid…

analysis.summary: API estimated a sharp 9.0 million barrel build in US crude oil inventories for the week ending November 6.
analysis.rationale: A large commercial crude inventory build of 9.0 million barrels reverses the prior week's draw and signals short-term oversupply, exerting downward pressure on crude prices.
